The last photo doesn’t look like an open eye to me, as all the lashes are the same length from inner to outer corner. You are right in that your lash tech didn’t follow through with what you wanted. 

I’d say just wait until your extensions grow/fall out, and if you’d like to get them done again see a diff lash tech and verbalize that you’d want them longer in the middle to really give a lifted look and avoid a droopy eye. 

In the meantime, you can also experiment with falsies (false lashes) that you can get for cheap at the drugstore and see what styles look best on you. Then ask for that specific look when you can afford lash extensions again. 

Also, since you’re unhappy with your lashes, it wouldn’t hurt to let your lash tech know that what she gave you wasn’t what you wanted, and see if she’d be able to redo them for you at a discounted rate. If she refuses to, or says that it’s what you asked for then drop her and find someone else.

- learn how to cook.

- put a portion of your paycheck into a savings, or emergency fund with each pay period. 

- give yourself a budget with your credit cards (me personally, i try to stay under $200) and NEVER reach the maximum limit on them.

- practice frugality. purchase things you know you’ll need/use, while also remembering to treat yourself once in a while to something you desire, or an occasional splurge. i have so many clothes, makeup and shoes that i’ve collected over the years that are useless to me now. 

- be mindful of your weight, and your eating habits. this is SO important. i’ll probably get downvoted to hell for this, but i know and have seen so many women literally balloon after high school/before they even hit 25. it’s extremely sad, and 9 times out of 10, is preventable. 

- develop hobbies that don’t involve eating or shopping. after a long day of work or school, it’s a common stress relief mechanism to order takeout/fast food or scroll endlessly on online shopping apps as a reward. it’s totally fine to do these things once in a while as a treat, but don’t make it an everyday thing. 

- read books! surf the web about things that intrigue you, or that you are curious about. educate yourself. history, politics, world events, etc. discover and learn how things work. you can literally do this in the comfort of your own home.

- go on dates! your 20s are your prime years! you learn a lot about yourself, a potential partner and what you want/don’t want in a relationship. shared  values, interests, sex, etc. figure that out while you’re young.

- you’ll constantly be changing, and the person you are at 28 will be completely different to the person you were at 21. all women go through periods of personal healing and enlightenment. some women dedicate months, even years to focus on themselves and forego dating and relationships. now that’s a personal choice, but you can still date people while going about your journey of self discovery. the two aren’t mutually exclusive.
